sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive rotation and Industrials strength are driving market breadth, but low agreement scores in Financials and Healthcare signal underlying fragility.

Industrials continues to pace the market, holding the top YTD rank with a momentum score of 0.733 and gaining 1 spot over the last 5 sessions. Broad market strength is concentrated in defensive and rate-sensitive areas, with 4 of 11 groups achieving "all-green" status (positive across the week, month, quarter, half, and YTD): Healthcare, Real Estate, Financials, and Consumer Defensive. Consumer Defensive (+1 spot, rank 6, momentum 0.45) and Healthcare (+1 spot, rank 7, momentum 0.68) both improved their standings this week.

Conversely, Utilities and Energy are fading. Utilities dropped 2 spots to rank 8 with a weak momentum score of 0.300, while Energy slipped 1 spot to rank 2 despite a momentum score of 0.450. Consumer Cyclical remains the deepest momentum laggard in the market, sitting at rank 11 with a score of 0.267.

## Strength
* **Positive Breadth:** 4 of 11 sector groups are currently "all-green," showing positive performance across all measured timeframes (week, month, quarter, half, and YTD).
* **Defensive and Value Core:** The all-green cohort is led by Healthcare (momentum 0.68) and Real Estate (momentum 0.58), followed by Financials (momentum 0.53) and Consumer Defensive (momentum 0.45).
* **Industrials Dominance:** Industrials remains the absolute momentum leader with a score of 0.733 and holds the number 1 YTD rank.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top Gainers:** Industrials (rank 1, momentum 0.73), Healthcare (rank 7, momentum 0.68), and Consumer Defensive (rank 6, momentum 0.45) each improved their rank by +1 spot over the last 5 sessions.
* **Top Losers:** Utilities fell the furthest, dropping -2 spots to rank 8 (momentum 0.300), while Energy declined -1 spot to rank 2 (momentum 0.450).
* **Momentum Extremes:** High-momentum leadership is concentrated in Industrials (0.733), Healthcare (0.683), and Technology (0.633), while Consumer Cyclical (0.267) and Utilities (0.300) lag furthest behind.

## Divergences
* **Fragile All-Green Sectors:** Both Financials and Healthcare are exhibiting unstable ranks despite their positive performance across all timeframes.
* **Low Agreement Scores:** Financials shows a highly divergent, fragile setup with an agreement score of just 0.30, while Healthcare also flags an early warning with an agreement score of 0.48.

- Communication Services - Watch the RS new high trigger to determine if the sector can maintain its 20-session relative strength leadership. risk_radar.relative_strength: Industrials and Technology lead the market with identical rs_score of 0.67 and rs_confirmed of 0.22, beating the S&P 500 on 5/7 and 4/7 timeframes respectively. Consumer Cyclical registered a positive RS cross, while Communication Services, Consumer Cyclical, Consumer Defensive, Financial, Healthcare, Real Estate, and Utilities all achieved new 20-session RS highs.

- Financial exhibits a fragile all-green setup with a very low rank agreement of 0.30, indicating underlying instability despite its recent 20-session RS new high.
- Healthcare also presents a fragile all-green divergence with a low rank agreement of 0.48, signaling potential weakness even as it beats the S&P 500 on 4/7 timeframes (rs_score 0.50, rs_confirmed 0.17) and marks a 20-session RS new high.

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Defensive leadership hardens as Healthcare and Food Distribution dominate the top momentum spots, while cyclical and energy-adjacent groups like Aluminum, Solar, and Uranium suffer sharp weekly rank declines.

Market breadth shows 33 of 144 groups maintaining all-green status across all major timeframes. Strength is concentrated in defensive real estate and healthcare, with REIT - Healthcare Facilities and Healthcare Plans leading the momentum charge. This defensive bid is supported by sustained buying in Food Distribution and Semiconductor Equipment & Materials. 

Conversely, rotation is punishing high-beta and resource-related sectors. Aluminum and Department Stores have plummeted in the rankings, alongside Solar and Uranium. While insurance and consumer electronics are catching strong short-term bids, several previously strong cyclical groups like Airlines and Diversified Banks are beginning to fade.

## Strength
* **Defensive Dominance:** REIT - Healthcare Facilities (0.84 momentum) and Healthcare Plans (0.83 momentum) lead the 33 all-green groups, displaying sustained strength across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.
* **Broad-Based Winners:** Food Distribution (0.82 momentum), Financial Conglomerates (0.80 momentum), and Biotechnology (0.83 momentum) remain perfectly aligned in positive territory across all weekly, monthly, and year-to-date metrics.
* **Sustained Tech & Consumer Footprint:** Semiconductor Equipment & Materials and REIT - Hotel & Motel continue to rank among the top 36 industries over the longer term.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Rapid Ascents:** Consumer Electronics jumped +33 spots to rank 56 (0.70 momentum), followed closely by Staffing & Employment Services (+29 spots, rank 47) and Publishing (+28 spots, rank 33).
* **Sharp Declines:** Aluminum and Department Stores both plummeted -30 spots to ranks 71 and 112 respectively, while Solar shed -28 spots to land at rank 105.
* **Severe Laggards:** Utilities - Independent Power Producers remains the weakest industry in the market with a momentum score of just 0.09 (rank 139), followed by Paper & Paper Products (0.14 momentum) and Pharmaceutical Retailers (0.19 momentum).

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** Airlines (0.74 momentum) and Banks - Diversified (0.69 momentum) are flashing warning signs, slipping -6 and -4 spots respectively over the last 5 sessions despite high momentum scores.
* **Emerging Bottom-Fishers:** Education & Training Services (+14 spots, 0.46 momentum) and Internet Retail (+13 spots, 0.46 momentum) are climbing rapidly in rank despite their subdued overall momentum.
* **Fragile All-Green Signals:** Medical Care Facilities (0.45 agreement) and Home Improvement Retail (0.46 agreement) are technically "all-green" but exhibit low structural agreement, making their bullish trend highly vulnerable.

pulse.headline: Weak breadth limits conviction as consumer electronics lead shifting industry momentum.

conviction.why: Market conviction is low given a weak 23% all-green breadth, 0.63 mean rank agreement, and 13 total divergences.
